content: Overview & Role NIST SP 800-171 / CMMC Readiness Checklist Specification The NIST SP 800-171 / CMMC Readiness Checklist ( slug: nist-800-171-checklist , CLIN 0003 — Cybersecurity & compliance, template family checklist ) is a static, browser-only readiness tool for defense and federal contractors. It lets a user walk through the 15 basic safeguarding requirements of FAR 52.204-21 (CMMC Level 1) or the 110 security requirements of NIST SP 800-171 Revision 2 (CMMC Level 2), record implementation status, compute a deterministic DoD Assessment Methodology (SPRS) score, and export a prioritized Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M) gap list. Scope boundaries: - Covers self-assessment tracking and deterministic scoring only. - Does not verify whether a technical control is actually effective on a live system, does not generate a signed affirmation, and does not submit scores to the Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS). - Does not cover classified information or NIST SP 800-172 enhanced requirements (CMMC Level 3).

title: Governing Regulations & Sources
subtitle: NIST SP 800-171 / CMMC Readiness Checklist Specification
summary: - NIST SP 800-171 Revision 2 ( Protecting Controlled Unclassified Information in Nonfederal Systems and Organizations ): Defines the 110 security requirements a...
content: Governing Regulations & Sources NIST SP 800-171 / CMMC Readiness Checklist Specification - NIST SP 800-171 Revision 2 ( Protecting Controlled Unclassified Information in Nonfederal Systems and Organizations ): Defines the 110 security requirements across 14 families (Access Control, Awareness and Training, Audit and Accountability, Configuration Management, Identification and Authentication, Incident Response, Maintenance, Media Protection, Personnel Security, Physical Protection, Risk Assessment, Security Assessment, System and Communications Protection, System and Information Integrity). Note: NIST published Revision 3 in 2024 (17 families), but DoD assessments and CMMC Level 2 continue to use Revision 2 unless a contract specifies otherwise. - NIST SP 800-171A ( Assessing Security Requirements for Controlled Unclassified Information ): Defines the assessment objectives and determination statements for each requirement. - 32 CFR Part 170 (CMMC Program rule, specifically § 170.24 DoD Assessment Methodology) and DFARS 252.204-7012 / 252.204-7019 / 252.204-7020 / 252.204-7021 : Govern CUI safeguarding, SPRS self-assessment scoring, and CMMC level requirements. - FAR 52.204-21 ( Basic Safeguarding of Covered Contractor Information Systems ): Defines the 15 basic safeguarding practices for systems holding Federal Contract Information (FCI) only (CMMC Level 1).

title: Inputs, Processing Logic & Outputs
subtitle: NIST SP 800-171 / CMMC Readiness Checklist Specification
summary: Inputs - Assessment baseline: CMMC Level 1 (FAR 52.204-21, 15 practices) or CMMC Level 2 / NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 (110 requirements) . - Per-requirement record: ...
content: Inputs, Processing Logic & Outputs NIST SP 800-171 / CMMC Readiness Checklist Specification Inputs - Assessment baseline: CMMC Level 1 (FAR 52.204-21, 15 practices) or CMMC Level 2 / NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 (110 requirements) . - Per-requirement record: - status : not assessed | implemented | partially implemented | not implemented | not applicable - notes : Optional local implementation summary (plain text) - poamOwner : Optional owner string for open gaps - poamTargetDate : Optional YYYY-MM-DD target completion date - Optional state import: JSON file exported from an earlier local session. Deterministic Processing Logic 1. Bundled catalog: All 15 FAR 52.204-21 practices and all 110 NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 requirements ( 3.1.1 through 3.14.7 ), family assignments, official DoD Assessment Methodology point weights ( 5 , 3 , or 1 ), and partial-credit eligibility flags are bundled statically inside the repository. 2. SPRS score calculation (NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2): - Start at 110 . - For each requirement: - implemented or not applicable : deduct 0 . - not implemented or not assessed : deduct full weight ( -5 , -3 , or -1 ). Treating not assessed as unimplemented ensures incomplete checklists fail closed and never inflate a score. - partially implemented : deduct full weight unless the requirement is explicitly eligible for partial credit under the DoD Assessment Methodology (for example, 3.5.3 multifactor authentication implemented for remote/privileged access only, or 3.13.11 non-FIPS cryptography in use, each carrying a -3 partial deduction instead of -5 ). - Planned items on a POA&M still incur full point deductions until their status is changed to implemented . - Valid score range is -203 to 110 . 3. CMMC Level 1 tally: Counts implemented practices out of 15 (all 15 must be implemented for Level 1 readiness). 4. Family rollup & POA&M prioritization: Aggregates counts and point deductions per family, then filters not implemented and partially implemented items sorted by descending point weight ( 5 → 3 → 1 ) so high-impact gaps appear first. Outputs - SPRS Readiness Score ( -203 to 110 ) or Level 1 Tally ( 0/15 to 15/15 ). - Family-by-family summary table showing implemented, partial, open, N/A, and unassessed counts plus points deducted. - Prioritized POA&M gap table ordered by point impact. - Client-side exports: Downloadable JSON (round-trip state), CSV, or Markdown summary generated in-memory via Blob URLs.

subtitle: NIST SP 800-171 / CMMC Readiness Checklist Specification
summary: Worked Example (NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2): - Baseline: 110 points. - Suppose 107 of 110 requirements are marked implemented , and 3 requirements have gaps: - 3.1.1...
content: Worked Example & Verification NIST SP 800-171 / CMMC Readiness Checklist Specification Worked Example (NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2): - Baseline: 110 points. - Suppose 107 of 110 requirements are marked implemented , and 3 requirements have gaps: - 3.1.1 (Access Control, weight 5 ): not implemented → -5 - 3.5.3 (Identification & Authentication — MFA, weight 5 , partial credit eligible): partially implemented (remote/privileged only) → -3 - 3.14.6 (System & Information Integrity, weight 1 ): not implemented → -1 - Total deductions: 5 + 3 + 1 = 9 . - Expected SPRS score: 110 - 9 = 101 . Boundary & Edge-Case Assertions: - All 110 requirements implemented → score 110 , POA&M list empty ( 0 items). - All 110 requirements not implemented → score -203 . - Fresh checklist with 0 items assessed ( not assessed ) → score -203 (never defaults to 110 ). - Marking a gap with a poamTargetDate without changing status to implemented leaves the score unchanged.

content: Overview & Role Offline Manifest Inspector Specification Offline Manifest Inspector ( slug: offline-manifest-inspector , CLIN 0005 — Tactical & DevSecOps) is a client-side static inspection tool in the ClearedStack catalog. On disconnected or air-gapped networks, package managers ( npm ), container runtimes ( containerd ), and security scanners cannot reach public registries, OSV/NVD feeds, or remote metadata endpoints. Engineers must inspect what is inside a container image manifest, a dependency lockfile, or a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) locally before importing artifacts into an enclave. The tool runs entirely in the visitor's browser with zero backend dependencies, making it available in both the Full Enclave Stack (Conn + Lazarette) and Snapshot Mode (frozen static bundle). Consistent with ClearedStack's architecture, it assumes containerd and OCI archives with zero Docker anywhere.

content: Governing Standards & Sources Offline Manifest Inspector Specification Every parser rule, field label, and digest check in Offline Manifest Inspector is grounded in public specifications: | Artifact Type | Governing Standard | Key Fields & Rules Checked | | --- | --- | --- | | Container Manifests & Indexes | Open Container Initiative (OCI) Image Specification v1.0 / v1.1 ( application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json , application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json , oci-layout ) | schemaVersion , mediaType , config.digest , layers[].digest and size , multi-arch manifests[].platform , and pinned @sha256: digests vs. mutable tags. | | Package Lockfiles | npm package-lock.json specification ( lockfileVersion 2 and 3) | packages entries, exact version , integrity (Subresource Integrity sha512- / sha256- ), and resolved URLs (flagging external public registries that must be mirrored inside the enclave). | | SPDX SBOMs | SPDX Specification v2.2 / v2.3 / v3.0 (ISO/IEC 5962:2021, JSON encoding) | spdxVersion , SPDXID , packages[].name , versionInfo , licenseConcluded / licenseDeclared , checksums[] , and externalRefs (PURL/CPE). | | CycloneDX SBOMs | CycloneDX Specification v1.4 / v1.5 / v1.6 (ECMA-424, JSON encoding) | bomFormat: "CycloneDX" , specVersion , metadata.component , components[].name , version , purl , hashes[] , and licenses[] . | | Cryptographic Hashing | NIST FIPS 180-4 ( Secure Hash Standard ) | SHA-256 file fingerprinting via the browser Web Crypto API ( crypto.subtle.digest("SHA-256", ...) ). | Scope limits: Offline Manifest Inspector performs structural parsing, digest computation, and local policy checks (such as flagging unpinned container tags, external resolved URLs, or components missing cryptographic hashes). It does not query remote vulnerability databases (CVE/NVD/OSV), pull container layers over a network, or make accreditation decisions.

title: Inputs, Processing Logic & Outputs
subtitle: Offline Manifest Inspector Specification
summary: Inputs - Primary artifact: Drag-and-drop file, local file picker ( File.arrayBuffer() ), or pasted JSON text for an OCI manifest/index ( manifest.json , index.j...
content: Inputs, Processing Logic & Outputs Offline Manifest Inspector Specification Inputs - Primary artifact: Drag-and-drop file, local file picker ( File.arrayBuffer() ), or pasted JSON text for an OCI manifest/index ( manifest.json , index.json ), package-lock.json , SPDX JSON, or CycloneDX JSON. - Optional expected digest: A sha256: string (for example, recorded outside the air gap from ctr -n k8s.io images ls or Lazarette) to compare against the uploaded file's computed SHA-256. - Optional format override: Auto-detection is default; the user may force a specific parser ( oci , npm-lock , spdx , cyclonedx ). Deterministic Browser-Only Processing Logic 1. Byte-level SHA-256 fingerprint: Computes crypto.subtle.digest("SHA-256", rawBytes) immediately in memory and formats the result as sha256: . If an expected digest was supplied, performs a constant-format lowercase comparison and reports MATCH or MISMATCH . 2. Deterministic format detection: Inspects top-level JSON keys without heuristics or AI: - bomFormat === "CycloneDX" → CycloneDX JSON parser. - spdxVersion present → SPDX JSON parser. - lockfileVersion present ( 2 or 3 ) and packages object → npm lockfile parser. - schemaVersion === 2 with OCI/Docker mediaType or manifests / layers arrays → OCI Image Manifest / Index parser. 3. Structured extraction & enclave checks: - OCI: Extracts config digest/size, layer digests/sizes, total compressed layer byte sum, and platform descriptors. Flags any image reference using a mutable tag without an @sha256: digest. - Lockfile: Enumerates all packages, counts sha512 vs. sha256 vs. missing integrity hashes, and inspects every resolved URL—flagging any non-internal host (such as registry.npmjs.org ) that must be mirrored before an offline npm ci build. - SBOM: Normalizes packages/components into a unified record ( name , version , purl , license , hashes ) and counts missing hashes and missing/NOASSERTION licenses. 4. Fail-closed error handling: Malformed JSON, unsupported lockfileVersion , or unrecognized schemas halt parsing with an explicit E PARSE diagnostic rather than guessing missing fields. Outputs - Summary header: Detected format and spec version, computed sha256: file digest, expected-digest match badge, total item/layer count, and warning count. - Interactive inspection table: Filterable and sortable list of layers, packages, or SBOM components with copyable digests and PURLs. - Exportable report: Deterministic JSON or Markdown summary generated via a local Blob URL ( URL.createObjectURL ) for inclusion in enclave transfer paperwork.

content: Overview & Role OSCAL Validator Specification The OSCAL Validator ( slug: oscal-validator , CLIN 0003 — Cybersecurity & compliance, template family validator ) is a static, browser-only tool that checks Open Security Controls Assessment Language (OSCAL) JSON documents locally without sending system security plans or assessment data to a remote server. It separates validation into three distinct stages—well-formedness, official NIST schema conformance, and internal reference integrity—so engineers know exactly why a file passes or fails. Scope boundaries: - Validates OSCAL JSON documents locally against bundled NIST OSCAL JSON schemas. - Does not fetch remote profiles, catalogs, or external href targets over the network (blocked by connect-src 'self' ). - Does not determine whether an OSCAL System Security Plan (SSP) accurately describes a real-world system; a file can be schema-valid and still factually wrong.

title: Governing Regulations & Sources
subtitle: OSCAL Validator Specification
summary: - NIST OSCAL (Open Security Controls Assessment Language) at pages.nist.gov/OSCAL/: Official JSON Schemas and model definitions across all three OSCAL layers: -...
content: Governing Regulations & Sources OSCAL Validator Specification - NIST OSCAL (Open Security Controls Assessment Language) at pages.nist.gov/OSCAL/: Official JSON Schemas and model definitions across all three OSCAL layers: - Controls layer: catalog , profile - Implementation layer: component-definition , system-security-plan - Assessment layer: assessment-plan , assessment-results , plan-of-action-and-milestones - RFC 8259 (JSON Data Interchange Format) and JSON Schema specifications used by the bundled NIST OSCAL schema releases.

title: Inputs, Processing Logic & Outputs
subtitle: OSCAL Validator Specification
summary: Inputs - OSCAL document: Local .json file upload ( FileReader ) or pasted JSON text. - Bundled sample fixtures: Built-in synthetic catalog , profile , and syste...
content: Inputs, Processing Logic & Outputs OSCAL Validator Specification Inputs - OSCAL document: Local .json file upload ( FileReader ) or pasted JSON text. - Bundled sample fixtures: Built-in synthetic catalog , profile , and system-security-plan samples for offline testing. - Optional version override: Defaults to auto-detecting metadata.oscal-version from the document; allows selecting from bundled NIST OSCAL schema versions (e.g., 1.0.4 , 1.1.2 , 1.1.3 ). Deterministic Three-Stage Processing Logic 1. Stage 1 — Well-formedness check: - Parses input with JSON.parse() . - If parsing fails, reports the syntax error message and position and halts Stages 2 and 3. 2. Stage 2 — Schema-valid check: - Detects the root OSCAL model property ( catalog , profile , component-definition , system-security-plan , assessment-plan , assessment-results , or plan-of-action-and-milestones ) and reads metadata.oscal-version . - Selects the exact bundled NIST OSCAL JSON Schema for that oscal-version . If the version is not bundled, fails closed with an explicit unsupported-version error rather than validating against a mismatched schema. - Runs the deterministic schema validator and collects every violation with its JSON Pointer path (e.g., /system-security-plan/metadata/last-modified ) and schema keyword. 3. Stage 3 — Reference & meaningful integrity checks: - Verifies that uuid fields match UUID syntax and checks for duplicate UUIDs within the document. - Verifies that internal fragment references ( uuid ) in import-profile , link , or rlink resolve to an existing uuid in back-matter.resources or the document's own elements. - Flags external http:// or https:// href references as info: external reference not fetched offline so users know external links were not resolved. - Checks presence of key metadata fields ( title , last-modified , version , oscal-version ). Outputs - Three-stage status summary: Pass/Fail/Skipped badges for Stage 1 (Well-Formed), Stage 2 (Schema-Valid), and Stage 3 (References Checked). - Detected document header: Model type, oscal-version , document uuid , and metadata.title . - Diagnostics table: Severity ( error | warning | info ), Stage ( 1 | 2 | 3 ), JSON Pointer path, and message. - Exportable validation report: Downloadable JSON or Markdown summary generated client-side.

content: Overview & Role Page Budget Planner Specification The Page Budget Planner ( page-budget-planner ) belongs to CLIN 0002 — Proposal & capture in src/data/catalog.ts . It divides a solicitation's hard page limit across proposal volumes and sections in proportion to Section M evaluation weights, after reserving fixed pages for introductions, summaries, or counted front matter. As explained in Answer every requirement, a page limit is a strict requirement: pages beyond the limit are commonly removed unread. content: Governing Regulations & Sources Page Budget Planner Specification - FAR Part 15 & FAR 15.204-1 (Sections L and M): Section L establishes volume structure, page limits, and formatting constraints (paper size, margins, font size, line spacing, and whether covers, tables of contents, acronym lists, resumes, or fold-outs count toward the limit). Section M states the evaluation factors and their relative importance (numerical weights or qualitative rankings such as "significantly more important than" ). - FAR 52.215-1 (Instructions to Offerors—Competitive Acquisition): Governs compliance with proposal preparation instructions and page-limit enforcement. - Solicitation-specific counting rules: Because solicitations differ on whether covers, TOCs, compliance matrices, and resumes count toward the cap, the planner models fixed reservations explicitly so the user can align inputs to Section L.

title: Inputs, Processing Logic & Outputs
subtitle: Page Budget Planner Specification
summary: Inputs | Field | Type | Constraints & Defaults | | --- | --- | --- | | totalPageLimit | Integer >= 1 | Total allowed pages for the volume (from Section L). | | ...
content: Inputs, Processing Logic & Outputs Page Budget Planner Specification Inputs | Field | Type | Constraints & Defaults | | --- | --- | --- | | totalPageLimit | Integer >= 1 | Total allowed pages for the volume (from Section L). | | fixedAllocations | Array of { label, pages, counted } | Fixed pages (e.g., Introduction/Executive Summary, or counted TOC/Compliance Matrix). Items with counted: false are tracked separately and excluded from the totalPageLimit pool. | | sections | Array of { name, weight, minPages? } | Scored sections/factors with relative weights (percentages or points, normalized automatically if they do not sum to 100) and optional minimum floor ( >= 0 ). | | roundingStep | Enum ( 1 , 0.5 ) | Defaults to 1 (whole-page budgets) or 0.5 (half-page increments). | Deterministic Processing Logic 1. Available pool calculation: - countedFixed = sum(fixed.pages where fixed.counted === true) - availablePages = totalPageLimit - countedFixed - Fails closed with a clear validation error if countedFixed > totalPageLimit or if sum(section.minPages) > availablePages . 2. Weight normalization: - totalWeight = sum(section.weight) (must be > 0 ). - share i = section i.weight / totalWeight 3. Proportional allocation & largest-remainder rounding: - Computes exact target exact i = availablePages share i , clamped to at least minPages i . - Floors each section to roundingStep ( floor(exact i / step) step ) and distributes remaining step units deterministically by largest fractional remainder (tie-breaking by highest weight, then section order) so the allocated pages sum exactly to availablePages and countedFixed + sum(allocated) === totalPageLimit . 4. Word-count guidance (informational): Estimates approximate word budget ( allocatedPages wordsPerPage , defaulting to 350 – 450 words/page depending on user-selected density) as a writer aid. Outputs - Volume Page Budget Table: Columns Part / Section , Working Weight (%) , Exact Share , Allocated Pages , Counted? , and Estimated Words . - Excluded Front/Back Matter Summary: Lists items marked counted: false (e.g., covers, resumes, acronym lists if excluded by Section L) so writers still track total deliverable length. - Local Exports: CSV and Markdown table exports for immediate inclusion in the proposal kickoff plan.

content: Overview & Role Prompt Payment Interest Tracker Specification The Prompt Payment Interest Tracker ( prompt-payment-interest , CLIN 0001 : Pricing & cost accounting) is a standalone, MIT-licensed static browser utility generated by Moldloft using the deterministic calculator stack template. It determines the statutory payment due date for a federal invoice, counts late days, selects the applicable Treasury semi-annual interest rate from a bundled rate table, and computes simple or compounded late-payment interest. The tool runs 100% in browser memory with zero backend services, zero runtime AI, and zero network calls after load. It also surfaces statutory deadlines for agency defect notices (7 days) and contractor written demands for unpaid interest penalties (40 days).

title: Inputs, Calculation Logic & Outputs
subtitle: Prompt Payment Interest Tracker Specification
summary: Inputs | Field | Type | Constraints / Options | Default | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Invoice Amount ( P ) | Currency ( $ ) | >= 0.00 | 20,000.00 | | Invoice Re...
content: Inputs, Calculation Logic & Outputs Prompt Payment Interest Tracker Specification Inputs | Field | Type | Constraints / Options | Default | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Invoice Amount ( P ) | Currency ( $ ) | >= 0.00 | 20,000.00 | | Invoice Received Date ( D inv ) | Date ( YYYY-MM-DD ) | Date proper invoice reached designated billing office | — | | Delivery Date ( D del ) | Date ( YYYY-MM-DD ) | Optional; used to compute 7-day deemed acceptance if D acc is blank | — | | Acceptance Date ( D acc ) | Date ( YYYY-MM-DD ) | Actual acceptance date, or auto-deemed D del + 7 days per 5 CFR 1315.4(g) | — | | Contract Payment Period | Integer ( days ) | > 0 (statutory default 30 days; shorter periods for specific commodities) | 30 | | Defect Notice Delay ( days ) | Integer ( days ) | >= 0 (if agency notified of invoice defect > 7 days after receipt, excess days reduce the payment window) | 0 | | Payment Transfer Date ( D pay ) | Date ( YYYY-MM-DD ) | Date of electronic transfer or check mailing | — | | Interest Rate ( R ) | Percentage ( % ) | Auto-selected from bundled Treasury semi-annual table based on D due + 1 day , with manual override | 4.75 | | Dispute / Financing Flag | Boolean | Excludes interest if amount is under bona fide dispute or is a financing/progress payment | false | Calculation Logic 1. Effective Acceptance Date ( D acc eff ): - Use actual D acc if provided; otherwise D del + 7 days (deemed acceptance). 2. Adjusted Payment Window ( W pay ): - penalty days = max(0, defect notice delay - 7) - W pay = max(0, contract payment period - penalty days) 3. Payment Due Date ( D due ): - D due = max(D inv, D acc eff) + W pay days 4. Applicable Treasury Rate ( R ): - Look up the semi-annual rate in effect on D due + 1 day (rate locks for the entire late period per 5 CFR 1315.10(a)(2)). 5. Days Late ( N ): - If D pay 30 (compounded every 30-day period): - Initialize principal = P , total interest = 0 , remaining = N . - While remaining > 0 : - chunk = min(30, remaining) - period interest = round to cent(principal (R / 100) (chunk / 360)) - total interest += period interest - principal += period interest - remaining -= chunk 7. De Minimis & Additional Penalty Rules: - If total interest < 1.00 : payable interest = $0.00 (5 CFR 1315.10(c)). - Calculate 40-day demand deadline ( D pay + 40 days ) and additional penalty ( clamp(payable interest, 25.00, 5000.00) if unpaid 10 days after D pay ). Outputs - Computed Dates: Effective Acceptance Date, Due Date, Days Late, and 40-Day Demand Deadline. - Period-by-Period Interest Table: Shows starting principal, days in period, and accrued interest for each 30-day (or partial) block. - Total Interest Owed and Additional Penalty Eligibility (with $1.00 de minimis and $25 – $5,000 penalty bounds). - Rate Verification Notice: Displays the effective date range of the bundled Treasury rate table and reminds users to verify against fiscal.treasury.gov/prompt-payment/ .

summary: The shredder is anchored to public federal acquisition structure and solicitation conventions: - FAR Part 15 (Contracting by Negotiation) & FAR 15.204-1 (Unifor...
content: Governing Regulations & Sources RFP Requirement Shredder Specification The shredder is anchored to public federal acquisition structure and solicitation conventions: - FAR Part 15 (Contracting by Negotiation) & FAR 15.204-1 (Uniform Contract Format): Defines the thirteen lettered solicitation sections ( A through M ), separating contract terms ( A – J ), representations ( K ), proposal instructions ( L ), and evaluation factors ( M ). Note: per Read a solicitation, the FAR overhaul underway since 2025 relocates and makes the Uniform Contract Format optional in draft text while FAR 15.204-1 remains in codified text; the parser supports both lettered UCF headings and plainer headings. - FAR Part 12 (Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services): Covers commercial solicitations that omit lettered UCF labels in favor of plain headings such as Instructions to Offerors (Section L equivalent), Evaluation or Basis for Award (Section M equivalent), and Statement of Work / Performance Work Statement / Statement of Objectives (Section C equivalent). - FAR 52.215-1 (Instructions to Offerors—Competitive Acquisition): Establishes binding submission rules, late-proposal treatment, and amendment acknowledgment requirements. - Solicitation precedence rule: The specific solicitation and its written amendments always outrank general conventions.

title: Inputs, Processing Logic & Outputs
subtitle: RFP Requirement Shredder Specification
summary: Inputs | Field | Type | Constraints & Defaults | | --- | --- | --- | | solicitationText | Plain text (pasted or local .txt / .md file) | Parsed strictly in brow...
content: Inputs, Processing Logic & Outputs RFP Requirement Shredder Specification Inputs | Field | Type | Constraints & Defaults | | --- | --- | --- | | solicitationText | Plain text (pasted or local .txt / .md file) | Parsed strictly in browser memory; supports UCF Sections L , M , C , H , J , and amendments. | | defaultSectionPrefix | Enum ( L , M , C , H , J , AUTO ) | Defaults to AUTO (infers prefix from nearest preceding section heading; falls back to REQ ). | | includeShould | Boolean | Defaults to true (treats "should" in Section L instructions as binding "shall" , per Answer every requirement). | | splitCompoundVerbs | Boolean | Defaults to true (splits multi-action clauses such as "shall design, test, and document" into separate numbered rows). | | startingIndex | Integer >= 1 | Defaults to 1 per prefix (e.g., L-001 , M-001 , C-001 ). | Deterministic Processing Logic 1. Heading & location tracking: Scans lines sequentially for UCF section markers ( Section L , L.4.1 , Section M , Section C , Section H , Section J , or FAR Part 12 equivalents like Instructions to Offerors , Evaluation Factors , Performance Work Statement ) and explicit page markers ( Page N , [p. N] , or form-feed \f breaks) to maintain current section , paragraph , and page state. 2. Sentence segmentation: Splits text into candidate sentences while protecting common federal abbreviations ( U.S.C. , C.F.R. , FAR 52.215-1 , e.g. , i.e. , No. , Sec. ) from false period breaks. 3. Binding-verb classification: Matches sentences against case-insensitive word-boundary patterns for "shall" , "must" , "will" , and (when enabled) "should" , and classifies the actor/role deterministically: - "The contractor shall" → Work duty ( C / H ) - "The offeror shall" / "Offerors must" → Proposal instruction ( L ) - "The Government will" → Government intent ( M / C ) - "should" / "may" → Preference or permission (flagged for reviewer verification) 4. Compound-action splitting (optional): When splitCompoundVerbs is true and a sentence contains a single modal verb followed by a comma/conjunction list of transitive verbs (e.g., "shall design, test, and document" ), emits one child row per action while preserving the full original sentence as context. 5. Exact-text preservation & stable IDs: Copies matched text verbatim without paraphrasing, assigns zero-padded stable IDs ( L-001 , M-001 , C-001 ), and records section , paragraph , and page . Outputs - Numbered Requirements Table: Columns ID , Prefix , Actor / Kind , Binding Verb , Source (Section / Paragraph / Page) , and Exact Requirement Text . - Summary Counts: Breakdown by prefix ( L , M , C , H , J , REQ ) and binding verb ( shall , must , will , should ). - Local Exports: Client-side CSV and JSON downloads (generated via Blob URLs in memory) formatted for direct import into the Compliance Matrix Generator ( compliance-matrix-generator ).

content: Overview & Role Section B Pricing Table Builder Specification The Section B Pricing Table Builder ( section-b-pricing-table , CLIN 0001 : Pricing & cost accounting) is a standalone, MIT-licensed static browser utility generated by Moldloft using the deterministic calculator stack template. It structures Contract Line Item Numbers (CLINs), descriptions, quantities, units of measure, unit prices, option-year escalations, and extended totals in the standard Uniform Contract Format (UCF) Section B layout. The tool runs entirely in browser memory with zero backend servers, zero runtime AI, and zero network calls after load. It enforces solicitation-aligned rounding rules (rounding unit rates to the cent before multiplying, or configurable unrounded multiplication) and exports clean local CSV/JSON schedules without transmitting pricing data.

content: Inputs, Calculation Logic & Outputs Section B Pricing Table Builder Specification Inputs | Field | Type | Constraints / Options | Default | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Rounding Mode | Enum | round unit first (round unit price to cent before multiplying by quantity) or round extended only | round unit first | | Option Escalation Rate | Percentage ( % ) | >= 0.00 (optional annual escalation applied when cloning a base CLIN to an option period) | 3.00 | | CLIN Row: Line Item ( clin ) | String | 4-digit or alphanumeric CLIN/SLIN (e.g., 0001 , 0002 , 1001 ) | 0001 | | CLIN Row: Period | Enum | Base , Option 1 , Option 2 , Option 3 , Option 4 | Base | | CLIN Row: Description | String | Solicitation labor category or deliverable title | — | | CLIN Row: Quantity | Number | >= 0 | 1880 | | CLIN Row: Unit of Measure | Enum / String | Hour , Month , Lot , Each , Year | Hour | | CLIN Row: Unit Price / NTE | Currency ( $ ) | >= 0.00 | 113.22 | | CLIN Row: NTE / Pass-Through Flag | Boolean | Marks plug/NTE lines (e.g., Travel) where unit price is omitted or fixed as a lot amount | false | Calculation Logic 1. Unit Price Escalation (when generating Option Year CLINs from Base Year): - raw option unit = base unit price (1 + escalation rate / 100) ^ option year index - If round unit first : effective unit price = round to cent(raw option unit) - If round extended only : effective unit price = raw option unit 2. Extended Price per CLIN: - extended price = round to cent(quantity effective unit price) - For NTE / Lot items ( quantity = 1 , unit = Lot ): extended price = round to cent(nte amount) 3. Period & Grand Totals: - period subtotal[p] = sum(extended price for all CLINs in period p) - total evaluated price = sum(period subtotal[p] for all periods) Outputs - Formatted Section B Table: Columns for Line Item , Period , Description , Quantity , Unit , Unit Price , and Amount . - Period Subtotals & Grand Total: Separate subtotals for Base Year and each Option Year, plus Total Evaluated Price. - Solicitation Override Checklist: Prompts the user to verify solicitation-specific rounding rules, labor category names, and whether travel/ODCs carry G&A or fee. - Local Export: Client-side CSV and JSON download generated via Blob URLs in browser memory (zero server round-trip).

summary: set-aside-guide ( CLIN 0004 , category: "market" , slug: set-aside-guide ) is a static, browser-only eligibility screener and reference guide in the ClearedStac...
content: Overview & Role Small Business Set-Aside Guide Specification set-aside-guide ( CLIN 0004 , category: "market" , slug: set-aside-guide ) is a static, browser-only eligibility screener and reference guide in the ClearedStack catalog. It helps businesses determine which federal small business set-aside programs they may qualify for, whether self-representation or formal Small Business Administration (SBA) certification is required, how solicitation dollar thresholds route competitions, and whether a proposed teaming split complies with limitations on subcontracting. As noted in Codes, registration and small business status, claiming an unconfirmed socioeconomic status in SAM.gov or on an offer is a false statement to the government. set-aside-guide surfaces the exact regulatory prerequisites before a user relies on any program.

title: Inputs, Processing Logic & Outputs
subtitle: Small Business Set-Aside Guide Specification
summary: Inputs | Field | Type | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | is small under naics | Boolean | Whether the firm (including affiliates) is under the solicitation's NAICS...
content: Inputs, Processing Logic & Outputs Small Business Set-Aside Guide Specification Inputs | Field | Type | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | is small under naics | Boolean | Whether the firm (including affiliates) is under the solicitation's NAICS size standard. | | program flags | Object of booleans | Underlying eligibility flags (51% ownership/control, HUBZone office/residency, designated industry) and active SBA certification flags ( 8(a) , HUBZone , WOSB/EDWOSB , SDVOSB ). | | estimated value usd | Number (optional, >= 0 ) | Anticipated contract dollar value for threshold routing. | | contract type | Enum ( services \| supplies \| general construction \| special trade construction ) | Optional contract category for subcontracting cap check. | | non sse subcontract pct | Number (optional, 0 – 100 ) | Optional percentage of government-paid amount planned for subcontractors that are not similarly situated entities. | Deterministic Processing Logic 1. Size Gate: If is small under naics === false , mark all 5 set-aside programs as Not eligible (small status under the solicitation's NAICS is mandatory for every program). 2. Per-Program Evaluation: For each program ( Small Business , 8(a) , HUBZone , WOSB/EDWOSB , SDVOSB ): - Small Business : Eligible now if is small under naics === true (via SAM.gov self-representation). - Socioeconomic programs ( 8(a) , HUBZone , WOSB/EDWOSB , SDVOSB ): - Criteria met + active SBA certification -> Eligible now - Criteria met + no SBA certification -> Potentially eligible — SBA certification required before bidding set-asides - Criteria not met -> Not eligible 3. Dollar Threshold Routing (when estimated value usd is provided): - Micro-purchase threshold (up to $15,000) - > 15000 and Simplified acquisition threshold (reserved for small businesses) - > 350000 -> Above SAT (Rule of Two applies) 4. Limitations on Subcontracting Check (when contract type and non sse subcontract pct are provided): - Lookup cap: 50% ( services / supplies ), 85% ( general construction ), 75% ( special trade construction ). - non sse subcontract pct Compliant ( cap -> Exceeds statutory cap ( > cap% ). Outputs - Program eligibility matrix: Status, establishment method ( SAM self-representation vs. SBA certification ), governing CFR/FAR citation, and required next step for all 5 programs. - Threshold routing card: Acquisition tier and default small-business reservation rule. - Subcontracting compliance result: Maximum allowed non-SSE percentage and pass/exceed indicator. - Exportable summary: Plain-text, Markdown, or JSON report for capture planning.

content: Overview & Role DISA STIG Reference Lookup Specification The DISA STIG Reference Lookup ( slug: stig-reference-lookup , CLIN 0003 — Cybersecurity & compliance, template family lookup ) is a static, browser-only tool for inspecting Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG) rules. Engineers and assessors often receive findings citing a Group ID ( V- number), Rule ID ( SV- number), product STIG ID, or Control Correlation Identifier ( CCI- number) interchangeably. This tool normalizes and searches all four identifiers offline, either against a bundled public sample benchmark or against a local DISA XCCDF .xml file opened in the browser. Scope boundaries: - Reference lookup and rule inspection only. - Does not execute automated SCAP scans, modify host configurations, or edit/sign .ckl checklist files. - Does not include proprietary or classified STIGs; users load public DISA benchmarks from their own workstation.

title: Inputs, Processing Logic & Outputs
subtitle: DISA STIG Reference Lookup Specification
summary: Inputs - Benchmark source: Bundled public sample XCCDF benchmark, or a user-selected local .xml XCCDF file read client-side via FileReader . - Search query: Fre...
content: Inputs, Processing Logic & Outputs DISA STIG Reference Lookup Specification Inputs - Benchmark source: Bundled public sample XCCDF benchmark, or a user-selected local .xml XCCDF file read client-side via FileReader . - Search query: Free-text string matching Group ID ( V-... ), Rule ID ( SV-... ), STIG ID (e.g., RHEL-08-010010 ), CCI ( CCI-... ), title, discussion, check text, or fix text. - Severity filter: All , CAT I (high) , CAT II (medium) , or CAT III (low) . Deterministic Processing Logic 1. Safe client-side XML parsing: - Parses XCCDF XML using the browser's built-in DOMParser ( application/xml ), which does not fetch external DTDs or resolve external XML entities. - Extracts benchmark metadata ( id , version , release-info , title ) so the user always sees the exact STIG version and release date. 2. Rule normalization: - Iterates every and child element, extracting: - groupId ( ) - ruleId ( ) - stigId ( element) - severity mapped deterministically: high → CAT I , medium → CAT II , low → CAT III - title , discussion (extracted from inside ), checkText ( ), fixText ( ), and ccis (all elements referencing cyber.mil/cci ). 3. Deterministic search & sort: - Case-insensitive matching across all identifier fields ( groupId , ruleId , stigId , ccis ) and full-text fields ( title , discussion , checkText , fixText ). - Exact or prefix identifier matches rank ahead of body-text matches; ties sort by severity ( CAT I → CAT II → CAT III ) and then groupId ascending. 4. Checklist status reference: Displays the four standard review states ( Open , Not a Finding , Not Applicable , Not Reviewed ) with a reminder that Not Applicable and accepted Open findings require written justification. Outputs - Benchmark header displaying title, version, release info, and total rule counts by category ( CAT I / II / III ). - Filterable rule table with Group ID, Rule ID, STIG ID, Severity badge, Title, and CCI tags. - Rule detail drawer showing Discussion, Check Text, Fix Text, and a copyable plain-text/Markdown rule summary.

content: Overview & Role Wrap Rate Calculator Specification The Wrap Rate Calculator ( wrap-rate-calculator , CLIN 0001 : Pricing & cost accounting) is a standalone, MIT-licensed static browser utility generated by Moldloft using the deterministic calculator stack template. It converts a direct labor wage or annual salary into a fully burdened hourly billing rate and computes both the cost wrap rate (without fee) and the billing wrap rate (with fee). The tool runs 100% in browser memory with zero backend services, zero runtime AI, and zero network calls after initial page load. It is designed for small federal contractors preparing time-and-materials (T&M), labor-hour, cost-reimbursement, or fixed-price labor estimates who need transparent, auditable step-by-step math.

title: Inputs, Calculation Logic & Outputs
subtitle: Wrap Rate Calculator Specification
summary: Inputs | Field | Type | Constraints / Options | Default | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Pay Input Mode | Enum | hourly wage or annual salary | hourly wage | | Bas...
content: Inputs, Calculation Logic & Outputs Wrap Rate Calculator Specification Inputs | Field | Type | Constraints / Options | Default | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Pay Input Mode | Enum | hourly wage or annual salary | hourly wage | | Base Pay | Number ( $ ) | >= 0.00 | 60.00 | | Annual Divisor Hours | Number ( hrs ) | > 0 (used when annual salary is selected; 2080 if leave is in fringe, 1880 – 1920 if leave is excluded from fringe) | 2080 | | Fringe Rate | Percentage ( % ) | >= 0.00 | 30.00 | | Overhead Rate | Percentage ( % ) | >= 0.00 | 20.00 | | Overhead Base Convention | Enum | dl plus fringe (direct labor + fringe) or dl only (direct labor wage alone) | dl plus fringe | | G&A Rate | Percentage ( % ) | >= 0.00 | 12.00 | | G&A Base Convention | Enum | total cost input (wage + fringe + overhead) or value added (selectable exclusion note) | total cost input | | Fee / Profit Rate | Percentage ( % ) | >= 0.00 | 8.00 | Calculation Logic 1. Base Hourly Wage ( W ): - If hourly wage : W = base pay - If annual salary : W = annual salary / divisor hours 2. Fringe ( F ): - fringe dollars = W (fringe rate / 100) - subtotal with fringe = W + fringe dollars 3. Overhead ( OH ): - If dl plus fringe : oh base = subtotal with fringe - If dl only : oh base = W - oh dollars = oh base (oh rate / 100) - subtotal with oh = subtotal with fringe + oh dollars 4. General & Administrative ( G&A ): - ga dollars = subtotal with oh (ga rate / 100) - total cost = subtotal with oh + ga dollars 5. Fee ( Fee ) & Fully Burdened Rate: - fee dollars = total cost (fee rate / 100) - burdened rate unrounded = total cost + fee dollars - burdened rate = round to cent(burdened rate unrounded) 6. Wrap Multipliers: - wrap rate cost = total cost / W (when W > 0 ) - wrap rate with fee = burdened rate unrounded / W (when W > 0 ) Outputs - Step-by-step build-up table: Base wage, Fringe ( $ and running total), Overhead ( $ and running total), G&A ( $ and running total), Fee ( $ and running total). - Fully Burdened Hourly Rate: Displayed rounded to the nearest cent ( $X.XX ) alongside unrounded precision for auditability. - Wrap Rate on Cost and Wrap Rate with Fee: Displayed to 4 decimal places ( 1.XXXX ). - Convention Warning Banner: Explicitly states which Overhead and G&A base conventions were applied and warns against mixing leave-in-fringe with reduced divisor hours (double-counting leave).

content: Worked Example & Verification Wrap Rate Calculator Specification Primary Fixture (from Labor rates and wrap rates ) - Inputs: Hourly wage $60.00 (or $124,800 / 2,080 hrs ), Fringe 30% , Overhead 20% on dl plus fringe , G&A 12% on total cost input , Fee 8% . - Expected Step-by-Step Output: - Base wage: $60.00 - Fringe ( 30% of $60.00 ): +$18.00 → Running total $78.00 - Overhead ( 20% of $78.00 ): +$15.60 → Running total $93.60 - G&A ( 12% of $93.60 ): +$11.23 ( $11.232 ) → Running total $104.83 ( $104.832 ) - Fee ( 8% of $104.832 ): +$8.39 ( $8.38656 ) → Fully burdened rate $113.22 - Wrap rate on cost: 1.30 × 1.20 × 1.12 = 1.7472 - Wrap rate with fee: 1.30 × 1.20 × 1.12 × 1.08 = 1.8870 Sanity Check & Boundary Fixtures - Round-Number Verification Fixture (from Check a tool's answer ): Wage $50.00 , Fringe 30% , Overhead 20% ( dl plus fringe ), G&A 10% , Fee 8% → $92.66 ( 50.00 × 1.30 × 1.20 × 1.10 × 1.08 = 92.664 ). - dl only Convention Check: With $60.00 wage, 30% fringe, 20% overhead on dl only ( +$12.00 instead of +$15.60 ), subtotal before G&A must equal $90.00 . - Zero Wage Edge Case: W = 0.00 returns $0.00 burdened rate and N/A for wrap multipliers (no division-by-zero NaN or Infinity ).
